top_news.title: ProToMEx: Rapid, Interpretable Explanations via Structured Representations
top_news.dek: ProToMEx introduces a new explainability paradigm using Probabilistic Topic Modeling to identify complex, combinatorial patterns in classifier decisions.
top_news.brief: Traditional post-hoc explainers often rely on simple feature attribution, which fails to capture the nuanced logic behind model predictions. ProToMEx addresses this by leveraging structured representations to articulate how specific combinations of features drive decision-making, offering a more interpretable alternative for complex machine learning models.
top_news.image_alt: Diagram showing the ProToMEx explainability framework architecture

top_news.title: H Company Releases NeoMME: A Family of 260M and 800M Single-Tower Multimodal Encoders That Drop the Vision Tower and Causal Decoder
top_news.dek: H Company's NeoMME models are lightweight, single-tower multimodal encoders that eliminate the need for separate vision towers or causal decoders.
top_news.brief: NeoMME provides 260M and 800M parameter models that process raw 32x32 image patches and text tokens within a single Transformer architecture. Utilizing a masked discrete-diffusion pretraining objective, these models support both dense and late-interaction retrieval, offering a streamlined approach to multimodal encoding.
top_news.image_alt: Architecture diagram of the NeoMME single-tower multimodal encoder

top_news.title: Show HN: Engrim – A universal, local-first SQLite memory engine for AI CLIs
top_news.dek: Engrim is a local-first SQLite memory engine designed to provide a universal, project-scoped episodic memory standard for AI CLI tools.
top_news.brief: Engrim aims to eliminate cloud lock-in for AI agents by using SQLite as a local storage backend. It is compatible with various AI coding assistants and CLI environments, allowing developers to maintain persistent, project-specific memory without relying on external proprietary services.

primary.title: Meta FAIR Introduces AI Research Preference Models (RPMs): Ranking ML Experiments Before Spending GPU Hours
primary.summary: AI research agents can propose far more experiments than they can afford to run. Meta FAIR, Oxford and UCL introduce AI Research Preference Models — frozen LLM judges that rank 15 unexecuted candidates and execute only one. On AIRS-Bench, the average normalized score rises from 0.684 to 0.729, and the baseline's 24-hour result arrives in roughly 15 hours. The post Meta FAIR Introduces AI Research Preference Models (RPMs): Ranking ML Experiments Before Spending GPU Hours appeared first on MarkTechPost.

primary.title: Google's WeatherNext 3 ditches physics simulations and learns weather directly from live satellite data
primary.summary: Google Research and DeepMind are releasing WeatherNext 3, a weather model that skips traditional physics simulations and learns directly from real-time satellite data. It produces hourly forecasts at up to five-kilometer resolution, five times more detailed than its predecessor. Google says regions in Africa, Latin America, and the Asia-Pacific that have lacked accurate forecasts should see the biggest gains. primary.summary: Researchers at King's College London and other institutions are examining whether "AI-associated psychosis" should become a clinical diagnosis.
